literal: Quan's younger brother Rang was Colonel of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Quan's younger brother Rang was Colonel of the Third Rank.

literal: Yi's younger brother Yi.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yi.

literal: Yi, styled Cigong, in youth was stern and dignified, had moral resolve, and with deep will loved learning.
idiomatic: Yi, styled Cigong, was stern and dignified in youth, principled, and devoted to learning.

literal: At the end of Great Dominion, through his father's merit he was granted the rank Baron of Pingchang county.
idiomatic: At the end of Great Dominion he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingchang for his father's merit.

literal: Later he was enfeoffed Duke of Guangdu county.
idiomatic: Later he was made Duke of Guangdu county.

literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was promoted Governor of Anwu.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended, he became Governor of Anwu.

literal: He devoted himself to promoting transformation and did not esteem punitive law.
idiomatic: He devoted himself to civilizing the people and did not rely on harsh punishments.

literal: There were men of the commandery, Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shuer, who disputed property and sued one another; Yi said: "This comes from the prefect's thin virtue and inability to bear up.
idiomatic: Two men of the commandery, Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shuer, sued one another over property. Yi said, "This comes from the prefect's thin virtue and failure to bear the weight of office.

literal: " Thereupon he took his household wealth and divided it between the two men, instructed them, and sent them away.
idiomatic: " He took his own household wealth, divided it between them, admonished them, and dismissed the case.

literal: Shan'an and the others each harbored shame; they moved their household registers to other provinces.
idiomatic: Shan'an and the others were shamed into moving their households to other provinces.

literal: Thereby customs were greatly harmonized.
idiomatic: Customs were thereby greatly harmonized.

literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Jianping commandery.
idiomatic: He was advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Jianping commandery.

literal: In the eras of Ming and Wu he successively served as Inspector of Xi Yan, Gua, and Shao.
idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Wu he held Xi Yan, Gua, and Shao in turn.

literal: Several times he followed in campaigns and was advanced to Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: He followed several campaigns and was advanced to Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, government and punishments daily fell into disorder; Yi submitted a memorial remonstrating the emperor.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, law and punishment grew daily more chaotic. Yi submitted a memorial of remonstrance.

literal: At the time Zheng Yi and Liu Fang, through favor and intimacy, held power.
idiomatic: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang then held power through imperial favor.

literal: They said Yi's words were not to their benefit and first spoke ill of him to the emperor.
idiomatic: They said Yi's words harmed them and first slandered him to the emperor.

literal: The emperor read the memorial and his color changed; he said to the attending ministers: "Yi is slandering the court."
idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, his face changed, and he told the attendants, "Yi is slandering the court."

literal: Correcting Master of the Left Yan Zhiyi advanced and said: "The ancient sage kings set up a post for slander and hung a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared not hearing their faults.
idiomatic: Correcting Master of the Left Yan Zhiyi stepped forward: "Ancient sage kings set up a post for slander and a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared never hearing their faults.

literal: Yi's words cannot be made a crime."
idiomatic: Yi's words cannot be punished."

literal: The emperor thereupon released the matter.
idiomatic: The emperor thereupon dropped the matter.

literal: When Wang Qian raised rebellion, Emperor Wen of Sui was planning to use Gao Jiong as commander; Jiong said Yi could serve as commander-in-chief.
idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Yang Jian meant to make Gao Jiong commander. Jiong said Yi could lead the army.

literal: The emperor was about to appoint him, but Liu Fang said: "Liang Rui's standing and hope have long been weighty—he cannot stand below Yi."
idiomatic: Yang Jian was about to appoint him, but Liu Fang said, "Liang Rui's standing is too great to serve under Yi."

literal: Thereupon Rui was made commander-in-chief and Yi made Campaigning Area Commander, commanding the left army; he defeated Qian's general Daxi Ji at Kaiyuan.
idiomatic: Rui was made commander-in-chief instead, with Yi as Campaigning Area Commander leading the left wing. He defeated Qian's general Daxi Ji at Kaiyuan.

literal: Soon he was appointed Area Commander of Tong Prefecture, granted five hundred slaves and concubines and three thousand lengths of mixed silks, and leap-promoted Senior Pillar of State.
idiomatic: He was soon made Area Commander of Tong, granted five hundred slaves and concubines and three thousand lengths of mixed silk, and leap-promoted Senior Pillar of State.

literal: After more than a year, because of illness he was relieved and returned; he died in the capital.
idiomatic: After more than a year illness relieved him of office. He returned and died in the capital.

literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Yu Prefecture; posthumous name Gang.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Yu, posthumous name Gang.

literal: He had sons Xuandao and Xuanmin, both of known name.
idiomatic: He had sons Xuandao and Xuanmin, both well known.

literal: Xuandao, styled Yuanming, by nature was careful and close; he did not associate with unworthy sorts.
idiomatic: Xuandao, styled Yuanming, was careful and reserved and kept no unworthy company.

literal: He served Zhou; through his father's merit he was granted the rank Baron of Cheng'an county, and held the post Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, Senior Gentleman.
idiomatic: Under Zhou, for his father's merit, he was Baron of Cheng'an and Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, Senior Gentleman.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, he was brought in as Outer Master of Troops.
idiomatic: When Yang Jian was Chancellor, Xuandao was brought in as Outer Master of Troops.

literal: When he took the throne, he was promoted Palace Scribe and advanced in rank to Viscount.
idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Xuandao became Palace Scribe and was advanced to Viscount.

literal: In his father's mourning he did not take water or broth for many days.
idiomatic: In mourning for his father he took neither water nor broth for many days.

literal: After more than a year he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to duty.

literal: When mourning ended he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and concurrently Right Guard Chief Commandant, Palace Scribe as before.
idiomatic: When mourning ended he was General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Right Guard Chief Commandant, retaining his post as Palace Scribe.

literal: Later he was promoted Deputy Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and advanced to Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: He was later Deputy Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Zhiyu was early of known name.
idiomatic: His son Zhiyu was known early.

literal: He went out to succeed his uncle Xuanmin.
idiomatic: He went out to succeed his uncle Xuanmin.

literal: Xuanmin, styled Zhongda, in youth was deep and close, with literary talent and thought.
idiomatic: Xuanmin, styled Zhongda, was deep and reserved in youth, with literary talent and purpose.

literal: At age eleven he went to Prince of Zhao Zhao's residence; Zhao ordered him to compose a poem.
idiomatic: At eleven he visited Prince of Zhao Zhao, who ordered him to compose a poem.

literal: Xuanmin composed the poem, with very much the will of secluded integrity.
idiomatic: Xuanmin's poem breathed secluded integrity.

literal: Zhao was greatly struck by it; seated guests none did not sigh in admiration.
idiomatic: Zhao marveled at it; every guest present sighed in admiration.

literal: He began his career as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and was promoted Thousand-Ox Guard.
idiomatic: He began as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and was promoted Thousand-Ox Guard.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent as envoy to comfort Ba and Shu.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xuanmin was Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent to comfort Ba and Shu.

literal: When he returned, he submitted a memorial, saying:
idiomatic: On his return he submitted a memorial:

literal: Your servant has heard that by opening the bedrock lineage the house of Han was thereby long enduring;
idiomatic: I have heard that by opening the bedrock lineage the house of Han endured;

literal: by establishing the secure rampart-city the fortune of Zhou was thereby numinous and long.
idiomatic: by establishing the secure rampart-city the fortune of Zhou remained numinous and long.

literal: In former times the First Emperor of Qin set pasture governors and abolished the feudal lords; the Wei of Later Han doted on flattering villains and kept kin at a distance—thereby the altars of state shifted to another clan and the sacred vessel passed to another surname.
idiomatic: Qin's First Emperor set pasture governors and abolished the feudal lords; Later Han doted on flatterers and kept kin at a distance—so the altars passed to another clan and the sacred vessel to another surname.

literal: This matter's clarity is brighter than watching fire.
idiomatic: This lesson is clearer than watching fire.

literal: Yet mountains and rivers set their barriers—none but kin should dwell there.
idiomatic: Yet mountains and rivers set their barriers, and none but kin should hold them.

literal: Moreover the soil of Shu is fertile and rich, its people numerous and flourishing; west it connects with Qiong and Bo, south it belongs to Jing and Wu.
idiomatic: Shu's soil is rich, its people numerous; west it reaches Qiong and Bo, south it joins Jing and Wu.

literal: When Zhou's virtue declined, this land thereupon became the head of the barbarians;
idiomatic: When Zhou's virtue declined, this land became the barbarians' head;

literal: when Yan's government lost control, this place then became the source of disaster.
idiomatic: when the Han house lost its grip, this place became disaster's source.

literal: Therefore the enlightened guard before form appears, and the secure control what is not yet in disorder—only then can one celebrate grandeur for ten thousand generations and exceed seven hundred years.
idiomatic: The enlightened guard before form appears; the secure control disorder before it rises—only then may fortune celebrate ten thousand generations and exceed seven hundred years.

literal: I bow before Your Majesty's sun-corner and dragon-countenance, bearing the fortune of the people's pushing upward;
idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's heaven-marked brow and dragon face, bearing the fortune of the people's upward push;

literal: matching heaven and assisting earth, occupying the season of yielding and yielding up.
idiomatic: matching heaven and assisting earth, in the season of yielding the throne.

literal: The hundred million fix their hearts; the hundred spirits receive their offices.
idiomatic: The hundred million fix their hearts; the hundred spirits receive their offices.

literal: It is right to plant and establish the screen of the realm, enfeoff and nurture sons and grandsons, continue the great design of Zhou and Han, and alter the overturned track of Qin and Wei.
idiomatic: It is right to plant the realm's screen, enfeoff and nurture sons and grandsons, continue Zhou and Han's great design, and turn from Qin and Wei's overturned path.

literal: Restrain the power of near intimates and exalt the root branches of the ducal clan.
idiomatic: Restrain near favorites' power and exalt the ducal clan's root branches.

literal: But the Three Shus and the Two Qis are anciently called heaven's barriers—to divide them among kingly kin, now is the time.
idiomatic: The Three Shus and Two Qis are anciently called heaven's barriers—to enfeoff kingly kin there is no better time.

literal: If the profitable establishment is fitting and the enfeoffment and planting obtain their places, then great villains will quiet their improper hopes and treacherous ministers will stop their crooked plots.
idiomatic: If establishment is fitting and enfeoffment well placed, great villains will quiet their improper hopes and treacherous ministers stop their crooked plots.

literal: The flourishing enterprise and great foundation will share heaven and earth in long endurance;
idiomatic: The flourishing enterprise and great foundation will share heaven and earth in long endurance;

literal: splendid fame and lush achievement will equal sun and moon in shining down.
idiomatic: splendid fame and lush achievement will equal sun and moon in shining down.

literal: Your servant, though his learning falls short of much hearing, yet his feeling is deep and his body is for the state—I venture this tube-and-bamboo view, trembling and scorched in the utmost depth."
idiomatic: Though my learning falls short of wide hearing, my feeling runs deep for the state. I venture this narrow view, trembling with the utmost fear."

literal: The emperor read the memorial and praised it; he said to Gao Jiong: "The Yu house for generations has had such men."
idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with praise and told Gao Jiong, "The Yu house for generations has produced such men."

literal: He finally accepted his words and sent Prince of Shu Xiu to garrison Shu.
idiomatic: He finally accepted the advice and sent Prince of Shu Xiu to hold Shu.

literal: Xuanmin constantly took the warning of fullness as the caution of former worthies valued; he always harbored the wish for quiet withdrawal.
idiomatic: Xuanmin constantly heeded the warning against fullness that former worthies prized and longed for quiet withdrawal.

literal: He composed "Rhapsody on Stating My Will" to show his aim.
idiomatic: He wrote the "Rhapsody on Stating My Will" to declare his intent.

literal: Before long he died in office, age twenty-nine.
idiomatic: Before long he died in office, aged twenty-nine.

literal: Yi's younger brother Li was Senior General, Inspector of Zhao Prefecture, and Duke of Anping commandery.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Li was Senior General, Inspector of Zhao, and Duke of Anping commandery.

literal: Li's younger brother Zhi at first was Opening Office.
idiomatic: Li's younger brother Zhi at first held Opening Office.

literal: Because he received Emperor Xuan's secret order, he reported Prince of Qi Xian's rebellion; he was thereupon enfeoffed Duke of Qi state.
idiomatic: Receiving Emperor Xuan's secret order, he reported Prince of Qi Xian for rebellion and was enfeoffed Duke of Qi.

literal: Soon he was appointed Pillar of State and held the post Grand Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was soon Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Works.

literal: Zhi's younger brother Shao was Senior Opening Office, Inspector of Sui Prefecture, and Duke of Huayang commandery.
idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Shao was Senior Opening Office, Inspector of Sui, and Duke of Huayang.

literal: Shao's younger brother Bi was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke of Ping'en county.
idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Bi was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke of Ping'en county.

literal: Bi's younger brother Lan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke who founded Xiangyang county.
idiomatic: Bi's younger brother Lan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and founding Duke of Xiangyang county.

literal: Lan's younger brother Kuang was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Lan's younger brother Kuang was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.

literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Heng Prefecture.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Heng.

literal: Discussion says: When the house of Wei pacified the central plains, Yu Lidi had military achievement through three reigns.
idiomatic: The commentators say: When Wei pacified the central plains, Yu Lidi won military merit through three reigns.

literal: Together with emptying himself to place himself below others and punishments not recklessly applied, this too is rare among the generals.
idiomatic: He also emptied himself before others and did not punish recklessly—rare among generals even then.

literal: Luoba took charge within and without and ended with merit and fame.
idiomatic: Luoba took charge within and without and ended in merit and fame.

literal: Lie by spirit and bearing was deep and far.
idiomatic: Lie was deep and far in spirit and bearing.

literal: Receiving appointment in a time of peril and danger, he had the substance of a pillar stone—perhaps a minister to repel insult!
idiomatic: Trusted in peril's hour, he had a pillar's substance—perhaps a minister to repel insult!

literal: Zhong was seen as close for his blunt simplicity; riding what was not his to hold, he thereupon monopolized awesome power, life and death at his own will.
idiomatic: Zhong won favor through blunt simplicity, then seized power not his to hold and made life and death his own.

literal: If it had not been the era of an empress, how could the gate and clan have been preserved whole?
idiomatic: Had it not been an empress's age, how could his house have survived whole?

literal: That he did not reach extermination and punishment was also his luck.
idiomatic: That he escaped extermination was luck as much as merit.

literal: Jin bore the strategy of assisting the age; he met the season of rising fortune, was a rafter beam for the great hall, likened to the boat and oar on the great stream.
idiomatic: Jin bore the strategy of assisting his age, met a rising fortune, was rafter beam to the great hall and boat on the great stream.

literal: He ended with venerable years and great virtue, reputation high and hope weighty.
idiomatic: He ended in venerable years and great virtue, his reputation high and his hope weighty.

literal: Rites were complete in the upper school; merit was sung in the Director of Music.
idiomatic: Rites were complete in the upper school; his merit was sung in the Director of Music.

literal: Yet he constantly took fullness as a warning and feared overturn and break—without a gentleman, how could the state stand?
idiomatic: Yet he constantly warned himself against fullness and feared overturn—without such a gentleman, how could the state stand?

literal: Yi was both son of a meritorious minister and by position a marriage kinsman; he bore favor through successive generations and together held civil and martial trust—principle was the same as sharing weal and woe, surviving and perishing together.
idiomatic: Yi was son of a meritorious minister and a marriage kinsman by position. Favor piled through generations; civil and martial trust rested on him together—his fate was bound to the throne's.

literal: Added to this, he held overall authority over war horses and received the entrustment of defending the walls; intelligence and ability were enough to guard against peril, power and force enough to stir the royal house.
idiomatic: He held overall command of armies and the trust of defending the realm. Wit enough to guard peril, power enough to stir the royal house.

literal: He never had the heart to release his post, but only pursued the meaning of following the time.
idiomatic: He never showed a heart to release his post, only the art of following the time.

literal: To exalt name and integrity in order to be noble and honored—is that what one hoped from such a man!
idiomatic: To exalt integrity and win honor—is that all one could ask of such a man!

literal: Zhongwen was broadly versed in documents and records and with heroic strategy made himself his own measure; in Yuchi Jiong's disorder he thereupon established merit and fame.
idiomatic: Zhongwen was versed in documents and records and measured himself by heroic strategy. In Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he won merit and fame.

literal: From then on afterward, several times he was placed at the hub of command.
idiomatic: From then on he several times held the army's hub.

literal: The Liaodong campaign in fact lost army and followers.
idiomatic: The Liaodong campaign in fact lost army and followers.

literal: This was the great tree about to topple—it was not the fault of a single rope alone.
idiomatic: The great tree was already toppling—it was not the fault of one rope alone.

literal: Yi's fortune met the time's coming; Xuandao and Xuanmin displayed their strength— the lofty foundation did not fall, split firewood could be borne—how flourishing!
idiomatic: Yi's fortune met the time's coming; Xuandao and Xuanmin showed their strength—the lofty foundation did not fall, split firewood could be borne. How flourishing!
